result.topic_en: Finding x such that xx+aa, xx+1 or x^4+1 is divisible by given numbers (aa+bb, a^4+b^4) using continued-fraction-type approximations, followed by Euler's prime-producing quadratic formulas x^2+x+17 and x^2+x+41.

Hinc etiam valores ipsius $x$ assignari poterunt, ut haec formula $xx+aa$ per eosdem numeros fiat divisibilis; sicque $xx+aa$ divisibilis erit per $41^2$, si fuerit $x=41^2t+378a$; ita hoc problema resolvi potest, quo quaeruntur valores ipsius $x$, ut haec formula $xx+aa$ divisibilis fiat per $(ff+gg)^2$.
Problema. Invenire numerum $x$, ut $xx+1$ dividi queat per $aa+bb$.
Solutio. Primo patet, si satisfaciat $x=\alpha$, etiam satisfacturum esse $x=m(a^2+b^2)\pm\alpha$. Deinde sumto $x=\frac{a}{b}$ satisfacit, quia fit $xx+1=\frac{aa+bb}{bb}$. Ponatur ergo $x=\frac{m(aa+bb)\pm a}{b}$, qui ergo numerus debet esse integer. Quia vero est $x=mb+\frac{a(ma\pm 1)}{b}$, debet esse $ma\pm 1$ divisibile per $b$. Quaeratur fractio $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$ fractioni $\frac{a}{b}$ proxime aequalis, quod fit si $\alpha b-\beta a=\pm 1$. Sumatur ergo $m=\beta$ eritque $x=\beta b+\frac{a(\beta a\pm 1)}{b}$. Cum igitur sit $\beta a\pm 1=\alpha b$, erit $x=\beta b+\alpha a$. In genere ergo $x=m(aa+bb)\pm(\alpha a+\beta b)$.
Problema. Invenire numerum $x$, ut formula $x^4+1$ divisibilis fiat per $a^4+b^4$.
Solutio. Primo patet hoc fieri, si $x=\frac{a}{b}$. Ponatur ergo $x=\frac{m(a^4+b^4)\pm a}{b}=mb^3+\frac{a(ma^3\pm 1)}{b}$. Quaeratur nunc fractio $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$ proxime aequalis huic $\frac{a^3}{b}$, ita ut sit $\beta a^3-\alpha b=\pm 1$, et sumatur $m=\beta$ eritque $x=\beta b^3+\alpha a$,
generaliter ergo $x=m(a^4+b^4)\pm(\beta b^3+\alpha a)$.
Potuissemus etiam ponere
$x=\frac{aa}{bb}$, fiat igitur $x=\frac{m(a^4+b^4)\pm aa}{bb}=mb^2+\frac{a^2(ma^2\pm 1)}{bb}$.
Quaeratur nunc fractio $\frac{\gamma}{\delta}$ proxime aequalis ipsi $\frac{aa}{bb}$, ut sit $\gamma bb-\delta aa=\pm 1$, sumaturque $m=\delta$ eritque
$x=\delta bb+\gamma aa$ et generaliter $x=m(a^4+b^4)\pm(\delta bb+\gamma aa)$,
quod ergo debet esse quadratum, cujus radix jam ante est assignata, unde patet hanc formulam
$m(a^4+b^4)\pm(\gamma aa+\delta bb)$
semper ad quadratum reduci posse, sive si omnia quadrata dividantur per divisorem $a^4+b^4$, inter residua certe occurret tam $\gamma aa+\delta bb$ quam $-\gamma aa-\delta bb$. Sit $a=3$ et $b=2$ et quaeratur fractio $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$ proxime aequalis ipsi $\frac{27}{2}$, erit $\alpha=13$ et $\beta=1$, hinc ergo erit $x=97m\pm 47$. Potuissemus quoque facere $a=2$ et $b=3$, et fractio $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$ proxime $=\frac{8}{3}$, quod fit sumendo $\alpha=3$ et $\beta=1$, tum erit $x=97m\pm 33$. Patet ergo tam $47^4+1$ quam $33^4+1$ divisibile esse per 97. A. m. T. II. p. 147.

methods.what: Solutions x for divisibility of x^2+1 (and x^2+a^2) by squares of numbers
Solving x^2+1 ≡ 0 mod a^2+b^2 via a near-equal fraction (convergent) α/β to a/b
Solving x^4+1 ≡ 0 mod a^4+b^4 via fraction approximating a^3/b
Second approach giving a square root of -1 type residue: γaa+δbb is a square modulo a^4+b^4

items.quote: ita hoc problema resolvi potest, quo quaeruntur valores ipsius $x$, ut haec formula $xx+aa$ divisibilis fiat per $(ff+gg)^2$.
items.english: thus this problem can be solved, in which values of x are sought such that the formula xx+aa becomes divisible by (ff+gg)^2.

items.quote: Invenire numerum $x$, ut $xx+1$ dividi queat per $aa+bb$.
items.english: To find a number x such that xx+1 can be divided by aa+bb.

items.quote: Invenire numerum $x$, ut formula $x^4+1$ divisibilis fiat per $a^4+b^4$.
items.english: To find a number x such that the formula x^4+1 becomes divisible by a^4+b^4.

items.quote:
unde patet hanc formulam
$m(a^4+b^4)\pm(\gamma aa+\delta bb)$
semper ad quadratum reduci posse, sive si omnia quadrata dividantur per divisorem $a^4+b^4$, inter residua certe occurret tam $\gamma aa+\delta bb$ quam $-\gamma aa-\delta bb$.
items.english: whence it is clear that this formula m(a^4+b^4)±(γaa+δbb) can always be reduced to a square, or if all squares are divided by the divisor a^4+b^4, among the residues there will certainly occur both γaa+δbb and −γaa−δbb.

items.quote: Jam autem demonstratum est, nullam dari hujusmodi formulam algebraicam, cujus omnes plane termini sint numeri primi.
items.english: But it has already been demonstrated that there is no algebraic formula of this kind all of whose terms are entirely prime numbers.
